name: development
summary: Plan with the owner, build test-first, review with clean context, land through a pull request.

phases.name: plan
phases.instruction: Read each record the change surfaced; cite those you build on in the plan's uses and list the rest in the plan's considered field with a line on why they do not apply. Interview the owner and fill in Problem, Outcome, Out of scope, UX, Data, Failure paths, Consumers and Lifecycle. Give the plan's `answers` beside its text: `ux` is none or mockups, `data` is none or stored, and `lifecycle` is none or record; each section holds the reason. UX says why there is no UI, or lists each mockup under ### Mockups with a ### Neighbours list; attach the owner's decision naming each mockup. Data says why nothing is stored, or run the understanding-check skill and attach its record and the owner's decision that references it. Failure paths has one row per step that can fail: what fails, the state it leaves, the recovery, and the order of the check against the destructive step it guards. Consumers lists every caller and reader of what the change produces or alters, and names the files searched. Lifecycle says why nothing changes state, or names the record `board changes lifecycle` writes and summarises its states in one line. Write the plan with `board changes plan` and attach the owner's signed plans/decision/v1 whose refs name the plan.

checks.remedy: List each mockup by URL or board path under ### Mockups in UX, with a ### Neighbours list, and attach the owner's plans/decision/v1 that names each in its urls or refs; or answer `ux` none in the plan and give the reason under UX.

checks.subject: data
checks.remedy: Run the understanding-check skill with the owner on the plan's Data section, attach its record with `board changes attach --path {change} --ref <record>`, and ask the owner to sign a plans/decision/v1 whose refs name it.

The plan's paths reach what this repository names as lifecycle code, so the plan cannot answer `lifecycle` none. Write the states, events and crash points by piping JSON with `path`, `text`, `doc` and `external` to `board changes lifecycle`, name that record under Lifecycle and answer `lifecycle` record.

Write the record the Lifecycle section names by piping JSON with `path`, `text`, `doc` and `external` to `board changes lifecycle`, or answer `lifecycle` none in the plan and give the reason under Lifecycle.

phases.name: build
phases.instruction: Start one builder in a fresh agent from `board changes brief --path {change}`; its first message begins with brief_line, then the brief. Read the lifecycle text the brief names, when it names one. Build test-first, commit, and record the head with `board changes attach --path {change} --head <sha>`. Attach each task. Run {suite} on the head and attach the run. Before advancing, ask the owner two of each understanding check's predict or edge questions again, worded differently, and add them to its rechecks.

checks.remedy: When {suite} is empty, the repository names no check suite: name one with `board changes attach --path {change} --suite /suites/<name>`, define one with `board runs define`, or ask the owner to waive this check. Otherwise run {suite} on {head} with `board runs run` and attach the run.

phases.name: review
phases.instruction: Review {head} with clean context: start a reviewer in a fresh agent with tools and a checkout of {head}, because the review plugin's run capability gives its model neither. Write a brief whose subject is the change, so the reviewer reads the plan as the spec, the lifecycle text the plan names and the rules on the plan's paths, and have it write a review/report/v1 at /reviews/<id>/report. Attach the report. The reviewer checks the Failure paths, Consumers and Lifecycle sections against the code as the review skill says: each Failure paths row has code that leaves the stated state and the recovery, and each check runs before the destructive step it guards; each Consumers search finds no reader the list omits; each lifecycle transition has one owner, no `_ =>` arm covers a state enum the record names, each crash point has a test, and the landed doc matches the record. The gate refuses a diff that edits a file outside the plan's paths; add the file with `board changes plan`, or revert the edit. Fix every critical or high finding, record the new head and review again.

checks.remedy: Only a reviewer can provide this: start one in a fresh agent with tools and a checkout of {head}, have it write a review/report/v1 for the change at /reviews/<id>/report, and attach it with `board changes attach --path {change} --ref /reviews/<id>/report`.

The change's diff edits what this repository names as lifecycle code and the change has no lifecycle record. Write one by piping JSON with `path`, `text`, `doc` and `external` to `board changes lifecycle`, or revert the edit.

The plan answers `lifecycle` none and the change's diff edits what this repository names as lifecycle code. Answer `lifecycle` record and name the lifecycle record under Lifecycle with `board changes plan --path {change}`, writing it first by piping JSON with `path`, `text`, `doc` and `external` to `board changes lifecycle` if it does not exist, or revert the edit.

phases.name: land
phases.instruction: Add What the tests prove and What the tests do not prove to the plan. Draft the pull request with `board changes pr --path {change}`, read pr.md and fix what is wrong, fix each path in `unreadable` and draft again or say why in the body, then run the command it returns in a POSIX shell from a checkout on {head}. Record the pull request with `board github ref --ref <owner>/<repo>#<number>` and attach it with --pull. Merging happens outside Board; advancing from land ends the change in done.

sections: What the tests do not prove

checks.remedy: The change's diff edits what this repository names as lifecycle code and the change has no lifecycle record. Write one by piping JSON with `path`, `text`, `doc` and `external` to `board changes lifecycle`, or revert the edit.

The plan answers `lifecycle` none and the change's diff edits what this repository names as lifecycle code. Answer `lifecycle` record and name the lifecycle record under Lifecycle with `board changes plan --path {change}`, writing it first by piping JSON with `path`, `text`, `doc` and `external` to `board changes lifecycle` if it does not exist, or revert the edit.
